sentences.text: In respect of an accident which has occurred on 24.08.2012, the insurer as well as the claimants are in appeal.
2. The driver of the car and J. Sunilkumar, who was an inmate of the car, were killed in the accident.
3. The claim petition was filed by the legal representatives of the deceased J. Sunil Kumar, who was an inmate in the car.
4. The insurer basically contends that the claim petition was not maintainable since the insurer of the car was NC: 2024:KHC:45628 not arraigned as a respondent.

It is also sought to be contended that as per the IMV report and the sketch, it was clear that the negligence was on the part of the driver and the car, and that the Tribunal had directly come to the conclusion that the driver of the lorry which it had insured was responsible for the accident.
It also contended that the sums awarded by the Tribunal were excessive.

5. Learned counsel for the claimants, on the other hand, contends that the chargesheet had been laid against the driver of the lorry and more importantly, the driver of the lorry was not examined to evidence the assertion of the insurer that the accident occurred as a result of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
It is submitted that the sums awarded by the Tribunal were inadequate and the same requires to be enhanced.

6. As far as the first contention of the insurer regarding non-arraigning of the insurer of the car is concerned, NC: 2024:KHC:45628 it is settled law that the claimants have the option of proceeding against the tortfeasors of their choice and the insurer does not have the right to contend the alleged tortfeasor is also to be arraigned as a respondent.
7. It may also be taken note that police after investigation have, in fact, laid a chargesheet against the driver of the lorry which was insured by the insurer.
It is therefore clear that as found by the police the accident did occur as a result of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.

sentences.text: It is also to be noticed that the driver of the lorry was not examined to ascertain the aspect of negligence.

It is to be stated here that the evidence of the driver of the lorry would become relevant,
more so when the car driver was also killed in the accident.
In the absence of the evidence of the driver of the lorry or any other eye-witness, the finding of NC: 2024:KHC:45628 the Tribunal that the lorry driver was responsible cannot be found fault with.

9. As far as compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.10,000/-
per month and has added 50% towards future prospects.
In this case, there is admittedly no proof of the actual income of the deceased J.Sunil Kumar.

In such circumstances, since the accident is of the year 2012, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which would be Rs.7,000/-.

Since the deceased was aged below 40 years,
future prospects at the rate of 40% requires to be added to the same, which makes his income to be Rs.9,800/- [Rs.7,000/- + (Rs.7,000/- x 40%).
Since the deceased was a bachelor, 50% requires to be deducted from the same, which makes his income to be Rs.4,900/-.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.9,99,600/- (Rs.4,900/- X 12 X '17' ) towards 'loss of dependency'.
11. The claimants, being parents and sister of deceased, would also be entitled to Rs.48,400/- each towards 'loss of love and affection', which would be Rs.1,45,200/- (Rs.48,400/- X 3 members).
They are also entitled to a sum of Rs.36,300/- towards miscellaneous expenses.

12. Thus, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.11,81,100/- as against Rs.16,35,000/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the from the date of petition till its realization.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

However, the claimants would not be entitled for interest for the delayed period as per order dated 09.06.2023.
15.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
16. The other aspects of the award of the Tribunal remain undisturbed.
17. The appeals are accordingly disposed of.
